action.message:
Implemented the fix in django/db/models/sql/query.py (only allowed file).

Change: In `Query.get_aggregation`, within the subquery branch's annotation-masking block, I now keep window-function annotations selected in the inner query when the query contains an over clause. Previously, when an aggregate referenced a window annotation (e.g. `Sum("cumul_DJR")` where `cumul_DJR = Window(Sum("DJR"), ...)`), the window annotation could be masked out of the inner query, causing the window function to be inlined into the outer aggregate and producing invalid SQL (`misuse of window function AVG()` / PostgreSQL `aggregate function calls cannot contain window function calls`).

The added logic:
```python
if self.contains_over_clause:
    for alias, annotation in self.annotations.items():
        if annotation.contains_over_clause:
            annotation_mask.add(alias)
```
This ensures referenced window annotations are materialized in the inner subquery so the outer aggregate operates on the window result rather than nesting a window function inside an aggregate.

Verification: scoped_tests on the `aggregation` selection passed — Ran 124 tests, OK (returncode 0). Note this is public regression verification only; host feature acceptance runs separately.
